points.name: Kingston, Jamaica
points.note: Turned from simple port into central hub 'processing' enslaved people; disembarkation, sale, reallocation; 1751–1752 nine factors; avg £30/person; enslaved-population value ~£25m.

points.name: Barbados
points.note: England claims 1625, settles 1627; 91–95% sugar exports; bagasse fuel; wind-powered mills (~400 pairs 1670; 219 estates WWI); land-limited, yield-preserving.

points.name: Hispaniola (Haiti / Saint-Domingue)
points.note: Spanish capture 1490s–early 1600s; French western third → Saint-Domingue 1697; Dutch sugar expertise.

points.name: Martinique
points.note: French colony 1635.

points.name: Guadeloupe
points.note: French colony 1635.

points.name: Jamaica
points.note: Spanish then English 1655; >95% sugar to Britain 1682–1701; sugar parishes enslaved pop. 6× 1720s–1788.

points.name: Trinidad
points.note: Captured by Spain 1490s–early 1600s.

points.name: Puerto Rico
points.note: Captured by Spain 1490s–early 1600s.

points.name: Suriname (Dutch Guiana)
points.note: Dutch Guiana; Dutch sugar-plantation model; then British/French adoption.

points.name: Essequibo
points.note: Dutch colony from 1616.

points.name: British Guiana (Guyana)
points.note: Steam-powered crushers in British Guiana; Dutch Guiana heritage.

points.name: Berbice
points.note: Dutch Guiana coast colony.

points.name: Curaçao
points.note: Dutch slave-trade network.

points.name: São Tomé
points.note: Uninhabited island; final transformation to slavery-based sugar plantation; aristocratic owners + Venetian/Genoese capital + African enslaved people; template transplanted to Brazil → Caribbean → North America.

points.name: Príncipe
points.note: Portuguese Atlantic sugar island.

points.name: Cape Verde
points.note: Portuguese extended slavery-based plantation model.

points.name: Madeira
points.note: Sugar cultivation spread to Atlantic islands; cane from Levant/Egypt; sugar masters from Andalusia; Merchant capital Venice/Genoa.

points.name: Canary Islands
points.note: Sugar cultivation; cane introduced from Levant; roundabout two-roller mill route possibility.

points.name: Azores
points.note: Portuguese Atlantic sugar island.

points.name: Sicily
points.note: First Mediterranean island sugar; enslaved North Africans after Black Death; Venetian/Genoese merchant capital.

points.name: Cyprus
points.note: Sugar cultivation; corvée; enslaved North Africans.

points.name: Rhodes
points.note: Sugar cultivation island.

points.name: Crete
points.note: Sugar cultivation; corvée especially; demesne land.

points.name: Valencia
points.note: Sugar knowledge crosses into Valencia.

points.name: Andalusia
points.note: Muslim-ruled Andalusia (800 years); sugar masters learn art; export to Madeira/Canary.

points.name: Egypt
points.note: Eastern Mediterranean sugar; cane source; bagasse practice in Mamluk period; Euphrates Delta enslaved revolt 9th c.

points.name: Syria
points.note: Eastern Mediterranean sugar; 'Holy Land'; sugar makers travel to Cyprus/Sicily.

points.name: Euphrates Delta
points.note: 9th-century Abbasid rebellion by thousands of enslaved East Africans on cane fields.

points.name: Pernambuco (Recife)
points.note: Brazil sugar region; Dutch occupation 1630–1654; channelled to Antwerp/Amsterdam refineries.

points.name: Bahia (Salvador)
points.note: Brazil sugar region.

points.name: Brazil
points.note: First to receive São Tomé model; land grants; Dutch takeover; largely Portuguese; abundant land.

points.name: Louisiana / New Orleans
points.note: Sugar plantations worked by enslaved labour; high mortality; gang system; centrifuge exception; beet sugar competition.

points.name: US South (South Carolina / Georgia / antebellum)
points.note: Cotton (and rice/indigo) enslaved plantations; task system vs gang; 'plantation value set by number of enslaved people'; enslaved as collateral; slavery's capitalism.

points.name: Elmina Castle
points.note: Major centre for purchase, confinement, shipment; Dutch capture 1637; later Dutch hub with asiento; 'womb of iron and gold' gun-slave-money nexus.

points.name: West African coast (Guinea coast)
points.note: Enslaved people bought in African ports; Indian textiles & saltpetre→gunpowder exchanged; Royal Africa Company; industrial-scale 'production' of enslaved people.

points.name: Royal African Company
points.note: Crown-owned; teamed with South Sea Company under asiento.

points.name: Lisbon
points.note: Largest re-export market for raw sugar; Dutch transport to Antwerp/Amsterdam for refining.

points.name: Antwerp
points.note: Biggest sugar refinery 16th c.; lost to Amsterdam 17th; refines sugar during Habsburg-Spain wars.

points.name: Amsterdam
points.note: Near-monopoly sugar refining; Bank of Amsterdam; guilder reserve; ~20% slave trade; Dutch East/West India.

points.name: London
points.note: Sugar refineries (sugar bakers) earliest industry; Great Plague 1665 relocation; major slave-trade centre; pound sterling; world financial centre; Hibbert Purrier & Horton.

points.name: Liverpool
points.note: Sugar refining; major slave-trade & shipbuilding port.

points.name: Bristol
points.note: Sugar refining; slave-trade & shipbuilding; Kenneth Morgan.

points.name: Glasgow
points.note: Sugar refining; major slave-trade & shipbuilding centre.

points.name: Plymouth
points.note: Sugar refinery.

points.name: Manchester
points.note: Major slave-trade centre; shipbuilding; profits into Lancashire cotton mills (Eric Williams thesis).

points.name: Portsmouth
points.note: West Indian ships used other docks to avoid contagion.

points.name: Potosí
points.note: Silver mines; enslaved & Indigenous labour; minted into real de a ocho; ~80% world silver 1494–1850 (with Mexico).

points.name: Mexico City
points.note: Silver; sugar re-export regional hub; asiento destination.

points.name: Mexico (silver)
points.note: Silver supply; asiento destinations; ~80% world silver with Potosí.

points.name: Bolivia
points.note: Bolivian silver mines; asiento destinations.

points.name: Acapulco
points.note: Western terminus of Manila galleon route.

points.name: Manila
points.note: Eastern terminus; Manila galleon links Spanish America to Philippines; silver→China.

points.name: China
points.note: Strong silver demand; silk/tea→Europe; cotton from India; later opium 1839–1860.

points.name: India (Bengal saltpetre / textiles)
points.note: Bengal biggest saltpetre; >90% European gunpowder saltpetre; cotton textiles→West Africa; land revenue pays; 25% sugar tariff after conquest; opium; 'Empire of Cotton'.

points.name: Bengal
points.note: Biggest saltpetre producer; ~90% European consumption; then British colony.

points.name: Venice
points.note: Merchant-finance for Mediterranean sugar; capital to islands & São Tomé/Brazil.

points.name: Genoa
points.note: Merchant capital for Mediterranean sugar.

routes.name: Europe → Africa (manufactures, guns, Indian textiles, saltpetre)
Americas → Europe (sugar, molasses, rum, cotton, raw materials, silver)
Caribbean raw sugar → European refining → re-export
Spanish silver → Europe → Asia (Manila galleon; China; India)
Internal slave trade in the Americas
routes.note: Disembarkation → holding yards/factorage → resale; second-selling; US South domestic trade.
